messages:
Emma L: Heads up — PR #8426 (docs/pricing) has examples for combined embeddings+generation billing. I think the numbers in the ‘tier crossover examples’ section are wrong when you apply reserved-capacity discounts.
Mike R: Can you paste the snippet? I want to see the inputs that trigger the mismatch.
Emma L: Sure — current snippet in the PR shows this toy example: 
```
Request: generate 512 tokens + 1 embedding vector (768 dims)
Billing shown in doc: generation: 512 * $0.00002 = $0.01024
embeddings: 1 * $0.0004 = $0.0004
Total = $0.01064
```
But our meter applies embeddings at per-embedding unit and generation per-token; the doc ignores that embeddings are tiered differently and that Dedicated reserved discounts apply to generation only for this account tier.
Lara (docs): Ack. Sounds like two issues: 1) the example math is oversimplified and mixes rate sources, 2) we need a clear caveat for Reserved/Dedicated pricing.
Nate P: Also, dashboard panels (usage -> cost breakdown) show a combined line item that customers may interpret as a single SKU. We should add a short note and a screenshot of the two-panel view: generation vs embeddings.
Emma L: Proposed patch: replace the toy math with a worked example that shows both list price and applied discounts, like: 
```
Example: user sends 1 request: generate 512 tokens + 1 embedding
List price: generation = 512 tokens * $0.00002/token = $0.01024
List price: embeddings = 1 embedding * $0.0004/embed = $0.0004
Subtotal (list) = $0.01064
Reserved discount applies to generation only (e.g., 30%): generation discounted = $0.01024 * 0.7 = $0.007168
Total after discount = $0.007168 + $0.0004 = $0.007568 (~$0.0076)
Note: rounding and billing units may differ depending on meter aggregation period.
```
Lara (docs): That looks good. Can you add an extra line that explains how our billing meter rounds tokens (per-request rounding to nearest whole token) and how embeddings are billed per-embedding unit? Also add a short code snippet for the SDK showing the request shape so engineers can cross-check with telemetry.
Emma L: Adding SDK snippet suggestion: 
```js
// client usage example (Node)
const resp = await redwood.responses.create({
  model: 'rw-instruct-1',
  input: 'Summarize the text',
  // embeddings call (server-side)
  embeddings: { model: 'rw-embed-1', inputs: ['...'] }
});
// In our billing pipeline this shows up as two meter events: `generation.tokens` and `embeddings.units`
```
Mike R: Nice. For the PR we should also wire in a short matrix table describing which discounts apply to which meters: hosted API (no reserved), dedicated (reserved generation, embeddings normally list), private (depends on contract). Keep it concise.
Lara (docs): I can add a 3-row mini-table and a small note about the Console panels to avoid confusion. Emma — can you add the numeric example and the SDK snippet to the PR? I'll take the table and the screenshot.
Emma L: Yep — pushing a small commit now. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/8426 :eyes:
DeployBot: CI status — docs/build: succeeded (link: https://ci.internal.redwood/docs/8426) :white_check_mark:
Nate P: Quick sanity check for the numbers: if Reserved discount varies by customer, should we show a generic 20% example instead of 30%? Safer to be conservative.
Emma L: Good point. I'll change to a 20% illustrative discount and mark it as an example.
Lara (docs): One more UX nit: change heading from "Tier crossover" to "Mixed-workload billing example" — clearer for readers.
Mike R: Sounds good. Also add a link to the metering glossary where we define `embedding unit` and `token` so folks can cross-reference.
Emma L: Done — updated PR with 20% discount, SDK snippet, and clarified heading. Ping me if anything else.
Lara (docs): Reviewing now, should be a quick merge. Thanks all :thumbsup:
